objects: active and inactive predictors; marginal and joint association
assumptions: single componentwise regression screening; correlated predictors
conclusion: SIS can prioritize correlated inactive predictors over weak active ones, miss marginally uncorrelated active predictors, and encounter collinearity difficulties.
scope: Three stated weaknesses of marginal screening.
span: First, some unimportant predictors that are highly correlated with the important predictors can have higher priority to be selected by SIS than other important predictors that are relatively weakly related to the response. Second, an important predictor that is marginally uncorrelated but jointly correlated with the response can not be picked by SIS and thus will not enter the estimated model. Third, the issue of collinearity between predictors adds difficulty to the problem of variable selection.
